heroHeadline: Federal Forces Repel VBIED Assault on Baidoa as Somali Pirates Hijack Cargo Ship Off Puntland Coast
heroSubtitle: Militia loyal to former Southwest State president Laftagareen — reportedly coordinating with Al-Shabaab elements — launched a pre-dawn VBIED assault on federal SNAF positions in Baidoa on August 17, 2026; federal forces used heavy weapons to repel the attack, killing 30+ attackers, though at least 2 civilians died in the crossfire, with fighting continuing into August 18 as remaining opposition fighters were cleared from the city. It was the fiercest fighting in Baidoa since the SNA's March 2026 takeover of the Southwest State capital, underscoring the unresolved fallout from Somalia's constitutional crisis over President Mohamud's term. The same day, at least 8 armed pirates hijacked the Cameroon-flagged cargo vessel Lutuf roughly 4 nautical miles south of Mareeyo on Somalia's coast; the crew was reported safe and EU NAVFOR Atalanta is investigating, while regional states under the Djibouti Code of Conduct move to stand up a new counter-piracy task force in response to a resurgence that an August 10 report put at 67 seafarers held hostage across four vessels — up from 44 across three vessels in mid-July. Elsewhere this period: President Mohamud presided over the graduation of roughly 3,000 newly trained SNA soldiers at a Saudi-funded training base in Galmudug on August 16 — the largest single graduation class since the 1991 collapse of the central government — as AUSSOM accelerates its drawdown ahead of the US ending UNSOS logistics funding after the mission's December 31, 2026 mandate expiry; AFRICOM confirmed its 78th airstrike of 2026 near Jilib on August 7; a Somali National Army truck was struck by an Al-Shabaab IED near Mubarak, Lower Shabelle, on August 10, killing 12-30+ soldiers per contested tolls; and Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur 'Jaamac' took office as Speaker of the Federal Parliament on August 12 after winning a boycotted August 11 vote amid the ongoing constitutional standoff.
